measurements.note: measured earlier on L40S as part of CUDA Graph capture investigation; CUDA Graph capture failed on this implementation due to cuBLAS incompatibility
hand-written CUDA kernel, no cuBLAS, standard cudaEvent-timed kernel launch
same custom kernel, CUDA Graph capture succeeded because it does not use cuBLAS; approximately 17% faster than normal launch, but still slower than CPU/AVX2

findings: C++/AVX2 is approximately 24-26x faster than Python/CuPy GPU eager mode (cuBLAS-backed)
AVX-512 gave no measurable benefit over AVX2-only on a 20x20 matrix; too small to benefit from wider SIMD registers

a hand-written CUDA kernel avoiding cuBLAS entirely allows CUDA Graph capture to succeed, unlike the cuBLAS-based implementation, but the resulting speedup over normal kernel launch is modest (~17%), because the remaining overhead is inherent to crossing into GPU execution (scheduling, synchronization), not just the CPU-side launch call that graphs eliminate
even the best-optimized GPU path tested (custom kernel + CUDA Graph, 4.12us) remains roughly 2.2x SLOWER than plain single-threaded C++/AVX2 on CPU (1.86us)

conclusive finding across four independently measured implementations: for this specific operation at this specific scale (single 20x20 matrix, one tick at a time), GPU execution is fundamentally disadvantaged versus CPU SIMD, regardless of how aggressively the GPU code is optimized

decision for the execution plane: Layer 1 (commutator computation) should run on CPU via AVX2, not GPU, at tick-by-tick granularity; GPU remains the correct choice only for batched/windowed workloads (UMAP/HDBSCAN/clustering re-fits), not the single-tick hot path
not_yet_done: no CPU pinning or real-time kernel tuning applied; current p99 figures are not representative of a tuned production deployment
the CUDA kernel uses a single thread block (400 threads); no attempt to test alternative GPU occupancy strategies, since the CPU result already conclusively wins for this component
